## RCA — confirmed at runtime on current `origin/main` (post-1957, post-1983)

### Ticket still stands after both landings

- **1957** (`irongrey-chubby-oxpecker`, aa7b) repaired the PRIMARY id-identity skip. It
  does not touch the comparison key, so the SECONDARY body-equality layer this ticket is
  about is unchanged — and it is precisely the layer that guards a lost map write.
- **1983** (`unreal-empathetic-illadopsis`, 5931) DID change what lands: `fit_preserving_marker`
  now reserves budget for `RECONCILER_MARKER`, so the landed body is
  `<content prefix><vendor notice>` re-decorated. The divergence this ticket describes
  survives and gained a SECOND component (the marker budget the differ key does not model).
  So the ticket is **not obsolete**; its mechanism is real and its numbers moved.

### Proven mechanism (driven, not read)

Driving the real Cloud objects (`_JiraSanitizer`, `AdfCodec`, `outbound_comments`) with a
43,200-char body on current main:

```
compare key len  = 32767   (sanitizer.fit_comment -> truncate_comment_body, PLAIN 32,767)
landed body len  = 31753   (fit_preserving_marker(decorate(b), AdfCodec.fit_outbound),
                            SERIALIZED-ADF 32,000, minus the marker budget)
EQUAL?           = False   (first divergence at index 31725)
```

In-limit bodies converge (short, multi-line 20k, unicode, empty all EQUAL); the divergence
is confined to the over-length regime, and it begins around **plain length ~31.8k** (where
the ADF serialization first crosses 32,000), not at 32,767.

### The good -> bad transition (discriminating experiment)

Re-ran the same two transforms at `27b868ba55^` (a detached worktree):

```
PRE-27b868ba55: cmp=32767  landed=32767  EQUAL=True
```

Before that commit both paths ran the SAME shared helper (`add_comment` called
`_sanitize_comment` -> `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body`). `27b868ba55` replaced the
send-path fit with `codec.fit_outbound` (the ADF/description fitter) and left
`_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment` on `truncate_comment_body`. That is the divergence, and it
rules out "pre-existing since 6afc".

### Defect legitimacy: `defect`, cited

`comment_limits.py`'s module docstring states the invariant as a hard requirement: *"If the
two paths used different truncation logic they could never agree on the landed body, and the
loop would persist. They MUST therefore share this one helper so they cannot drift."*
`_diff_comments`'s own docstring asserts "the send path truncates an over-length body to
Jira's 32,767-char limit" — a statement that is now FALSE.

### Defect origin

`caused_by` = **789c-1251-fc21-4cf6** (`emersed-specific-mutt`), commit `27b868ba55`,
2026-08-13. Not the file the fix lands in and not a blame-majority answer: this is the change
that moved the send path off the shared fitter while the differ stayed on it. Its own review
demoted body-equality to SECONDARY in the same commit, so it is exactly the work item where
the divergence could have been caught. Close class: `regression`.

### A THIRD, separate divergence found (not this ticket)

This project runs `rich_text_cutover = "cloud"` (rebar.toml:87), i.e. rich mode is ON. Under
rich the local key is normalized with `AdfCodec.normalize_outbound` (markdown round trip,
which ESCAPES `[`/`]`) while the Jira side is decoded with `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`
(`adf_to_text`, no escaping). So a markdown comment WELL WITHIN the limit already fails
body-equality today:

```
rich=True, in-limit markdown:  local '[link](<http://x>)'  vs landed '[link](http://x)'   -> no match
```

That is a decode asymmetry, not a fit divergence, so it is out of this ticket's scope. Filing
it separately with `discovered_from`.

comments.body:
## Debug report — fix pushed as Gerrit change 1993

**Problem.** The Cloud outbound comment differ's body-equality dedup key was fitted with a
different rule than the send path, so for an over-length comment it could never match.

**Proven root cause.** `_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment` (`adapters/jira/backend.py`) returned
`comment_limits.truncate_comment_body` — a PLAIN 32,767-character cap — while
`acli_cli_ops.add_comment` fits with `fit_preserving_marker(decorate(body),
AdfCodec.fit_outbound)`, which measures the SERIALIZED ADF against 32,000 and reserves budget
for `RECONCILER_MARKER`. Driven on current main with a 43,200-char body: key 32,767, landed
31,753, first divergence at index 31,725. The window opens around plain length ~31.8k (where
the ADF serialization first crosses its budget), not at 32,767.

**Proof / discriminating experiment.** Re-ran both transforms at `27b868ba55^`: `cmp=32767
landed=32767 EQUAL=True`. Before that commit both paths ran the one shared helper. That dates
the transition and rules out "pre-existing since 6afc".

**Defect origin.** `caused_by` = `789c-1251-fc21-4cf6` (`emersed-specific-mutt`), commit
`27b868ba55`. Recorded as a link; will be passed explicitly on the close. Class: `regression`.
Note the attribution is NOT the file the fix lands in and not a blame-majority answer — that
commit moved the send path off the shared fitter and left the differ on it, and it demoted
body-equality to SECONDARY in the same change, so it is exactly where a reviewer could have
caught this.

**Did 1957 / 1983 overtake it?** No.
- 1957 (`aa7b`) repaired the PRIMARY id-identity skip and does not touch the comparison key.
- 1983 (`5931`) DID change the landed body — `fit_preserving_marker` now reserves marker
  budget — so the divergence gained a SECOND component that the differ key also did not model.
  Both components are fixed here. Not obsolete.

**Fix.** `outbound_comments.fit_comment_as_sent(text, fit)` (new, beside `fit_preserving_marker`,
vendor fitter injected as a `Callable`) returns the marker-free text the send path lands;
Cloud's `fit_comment` composes it with the flag-governed `AdfCodec`. `_diff_comments`, Data
Center, `comment_limits.py` and every send path are untouched — bug 049e deliberately keeps
DC's comment ceiling distinct from its description fitter, so the convergence is restored
per-backend rather than by coupling the shared layer to a codec.

**Migration / blast radius: none, and it cannot re-post.** The dedup key is computed in memory
each pass and is never persisted (`binding_store` maps `local_comment_key` -> Jira comment id,
never a body or hash), so there is no stored key to migrate. Over a corpus (short, multi-line
20k, markdown, unicode, empty, 32,200, 31,800, 43k, 60k) in both rich modes, **every case where
the old key matched the landed body, the new key matches it too** — the change can only ADD
dedup skips, never remove one.

**RED -> GREEN + mutation.** `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_comment_dedup_key_matches_send_fit.py`
— 5 failed / 3 passed before the fix (the 3 are its own guards), 8 passed after. Held out of the
fixer's tree entirely (moved off-disk, path declared off-limits). Returned to RED under two
seeded mutations: restoring `truncate_comment_body`, and dropping the marker budget (bare
`fit_outbound`). Restored -> GREEN.

**Two existing tests retargeted, not weakened.** Both pinned the model of the send path that
`27b868ba55` invalidated: the held-out port oracle compared `fit_comment` against
`truncate_comment_body`, and the two-pass convergence test simulated the landed body with it —
which is why that convergence test stayed green while live convergence was broken. Both now
derive their expectation from the real send path, both keep every original assertion (the port
oracle gains one), and both were confirmed RED under a seeded revert.

**Gates.** `make lint`, `make typecheck` (616 files), complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0
stale=0`, the five repo oracles (`check_wall_clock_asserts`, `check_raw_git_writes`,
`check_comment_hygiene`, `check_docs_index`, `check_config_reads`), and the full unit sweep:
**8739 passed, 15 skipped**.

**Caller-dependency sweep.** Cloud's `fit_comment` has exactly one production consumer
(`_diff_comments`, via the `FieldSanitizer` port). No production caller depends on the old
plain-cap behaviour. The only behavioural dependencies were the two tests above.

**Sibling sweep.**
- *Construct axis* — "a differ comparison key fitted differently from its send path". Only two
  comment fitters exist. Data Center's is already pinned byte-identical to its own send path
  (`test_dc_backend_characterization.py`, `test_dc_comment_ceiling_049e.py`). The description
  path uses the same `fit_outbound` on both sides and is never marker-decorated, so the
  marker-budget component cannot arise there. No further live instances.
- *Parity axis* — the rule is "the outbound comparison key must be the text the send path
  lands". Cloud: FIXED. DC: the send path's own comment fitting is the subject of the queued
  `community-sediment-snipe`; this change deliberately does not absorb it and leaves DC
  byte-identical. Create path (`_map_comments_for_create`) goes through the same `add_comment`
  and the same differ, so it is covered. Inbound direction is marker-based (repaired by 5931),
  not fit-based — N/A.

**Residual risk.**
- *Ticket filed* — `aragonite-bleached-vipersquid` (`17c3-2f6e-a5e0-438c`, linked
  `discovered_from`): under this project's `rich_text_cutover = "cloud"` the local key is
  markdown-decoded (`AdfCodec.normalize_outbound`, which escapes `[`/`]`) while the Jira side is
  decoded with `adf_to_text`. An IN-LIMIT markdown comment already fails body equality today for
  that reason, so it is a strictly wider blast radius than this fit divergence and is not fixed
  here.
- *Accepted* — Cloud's `_JiraSanitizer.sanitize_comment` -> `jira_fields._sanitize_comment` has
  had no live production caller since `27b868ba55` removed it from `add_comment`; it is now an
  orphan on the Cloud side. Pre-existing, not touched, out of scope for a bug fix.

**Replication.** The original report's runtime evidence no longer reproduces: driving both paths
on the fixed tree, `fit_comment` returns exactly the 31,753-char text the send path lands, and a
second differ pass over the landed body emits zero mutations.

comments.body:
## The code-review advisory was RIGHT — the test was measuring the helper, not the convergence

The `LLM-Review +1` on change 1993 carried one advisory: the new test rebuilds its expectation
from the same helper the fix uses. I tried it rather than reasoning about it, and it was a real
hole — the same one this ticket's RCA criticises one commit generation earlier.

### 1. Did the two sides derive independently? NO (as originally written)

The first version computed the send side as
`fit_preserving_marker(_decorate_outbound_comment(body), codec.fit_outbound)` — a
RE-DERIVATION of what `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` happens to do today, not a call to it. The fix
(`fit_comment_as_sent`) is that same composition. So the assertion compared one composition
against a copy of itself.

That is precisely the failure mode this ticket already documented: the old
`mutate/test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py` modelled the landed body as
`comment_limits.truncate_comment_body(emitted)`, and when `27b868ba55` moved the send path off
that helper the model went silently stale while the test stayed green.

### 2. Did the mutation check discriminate? NO — and this is the sharp finding

The two mutations I originally reported (restore `truncate_comment_body`; drop the marker
budget) both hit the DIFFER side only, so both went RED and looked convincing. The mutation
that matters is the one on the SEND side — the drift that *is* this ticket's regression:

```
MUT A: add_comment: fit_preserving_marker(body, codec.fit_outbound) -> codec.fit_outbound(body)
       (i.e. re-commit 27b868ba55's exact mistake)
       ORIGINAL TEST: 8 passed   <-- GREEN against the very regression it is named for
```

A test that cannot detect its own bug being re-introduced from the other side is not an oracle.

### The strengthening

`_send()` now DRIVES the real `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` with only `_run_acli` stubbed and
CAPTURES the `--body` argument off the command line. Everything between `add_comment`'s
signature and the wire is real, so the send side of the assertion moves with the send path
instead of with a copy of it. The two sides now meet only at the assertion: left is the
differ's `_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment`, right is decoded from the captured wire body.

The AC-1 test is also now parametrized over `rich_text_cutover` via its canonical env override
(`off` and `cloud`) instead of over a locally constructed codec, so the flag's real resolution
path runs on both sides.

### Kill matrix after the strengthening (each mutation applied, run, reverted)

| # | Mutation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | send path drifts off the shared helper (`27b868ba55` re-committed) | **GREEN** | **RED** |
| B | differ side reverts to `truncate_comment_body` (the root cause) | RED | RED |
| C | differ side drops the marker budget (bare `fit_outbound`) | RED | RED |
| D | inside the shared `fit_preserving_marker` (both sides move in step) | GREEN | GREEN |

### On D, stated plainly rather than explained away

D shrinks the binary search's kept prefix by 7 characters. It is killed by **nothing** — not
this file, and not the wider comment suite (`marker_survives_truncation`,
`length_convergence`, `richtext_port_heldout`: 18 passed under D). I am calling it an
equivalent mutant, not a covered case: it violates no contract anyone states. The body still
carries its marker, still fits the budget, and both sides still agree — no assertion in the
repo says the retained prefix must be MAXIMAL. Killing it would need a new "fits as much as
possible" contract, which is a widening, not a bug fix. Recorded here so the next reader sees
it was measured and judged rather than missed.

Worth noting for D's converse: convergence genuinely IS preserved when the shared helper
changes, because both sides call it. That is what "share one function so they cannot drift"
buys, and it is why A — not D — is the mutation that had to go red.

`state/test_richtext_port_heldout.py` still re-derives from the helpers (it is a port-level
characterization of `fit_comment`, and it stays GREEN under A). Its docstring now says so
explicitly and points at the diffing test for the drift discrimination, so it is not mistaken
for the convergence oracle.

comments.body:
## Patchset 2 on Gerrit 1993 — two process findings worth recording

### The local sweep caught something CI's `Verified +1` did not

Patchset 1 earned BOTH `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`. Running the full local unit sweep
against the strengthened tree then failed
`tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py::test_the_real_tree_is_clean`:

```
comment-hygiene: 1 rot-prone reference(s) found
  .../test_comment_dedup_key_matches_send_fit.py  [commit-sha]  27b868ba55
```

The bare commit sha was present in patchset 1's test file too, in the same docstring — so a
tree that CI voted `Verified +1` on carried a hygiene violation the local sweep rejects. Not
investigated further (out of scope for this ticket), but flagged: whatever selection CI uses
for that guard did not exercise it here, so a green `Verified` is not evidence the guard passed.
Fixed by citing the ticket (`emersed-specific-mutt`) instead of the sha in all four places,
which is also what AGENTS.md asks for.

### I hit the duplicate-change trap AGENTS.md documents, and caught it on the trailer check

Amending with `git commit --amend -F <file>` REPLACED the whole message, dropping the
`Change-Id`; the `commit-msg` hook then stamped a fresh one
(`I51d760e9...` -> `Ice17b4da...`). Pushing that would have opened a DUPLICATE change rather
than a patchset — exactly the failure `make amend-msg` exists to prevent, and exactly what
AGENTS.md says not to do. Caught by checking `git log -1 --format='%(trailers)'` after the
amend rather than by pushing and seeing.

Recovered by putting the ORIGINAL `Change-Id` and the `Signed-off-by` back into the message
file explicitly. A second trap followed immediately: a blank line before the `Change-Id` split
`rebar-ticket:` into its own trailer block, so `%(trailers)` no longer carried it and the CI
ticket gate would have failed. Consolidated into one block and confirmed with
`rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev HEAD` -> `OK - resolved e339-9709-15fe-419a`.

The push landed as **patchset 2 of 1993** with both approvals correctly outdated and removed —
confirming it is a patchset, not a duplicate.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## CORRECTION — retracting the "CI gap" claim in my previous comment

My previous comment asserted that patchset 1 earned `Verified +1` on a tree carrying a
comment-hygiene violation, and suggested "whatever selection CI uses for that guard did not
exercise it here". **That is wrong. Disregard it. There is no CI gap.** Recording the
retraction here because a wrong finding in the ticket record is worse than a missing one —
someone acts on it.

### What I verified this time, instead of inferring

1. **Patchset 1's tree is clean.** Fetched `refs/changes/93/1993/1` (`c11dd21173f4`) into its
   own worktree and ran the gate directly: `python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` -> **exit
   0**, and `grep -rn 27b868ba55 src tests` -> **3 occurrences**. The sha was in patchset 1 and
   the tree passed anyway.
2. **CI does run the gate**, in the reusable that gates both lanes:
   `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, step "comment-hygiene gate" ->
   `python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py`.
3. **The guard is BLOCK-scoped, not token-scoped.** Its own header
   (`scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py:10-14`): a triggering block "is ACCEPTED when it cites a
   durable reference: a grouped hex ticket id, a word-triple store alias, an ADR id, or
   `context: external`". Confirmed with a controlled A/B probe — the SAME sha in two docstrings:

   ```
   """Commit ``27b868ba55`` moved the send path ..."""              -> 1 rot-prone reference found
   """Bug e339-9709-15fe-419a: commit ``27b868ba55`` moved ..."""   -> clean
   ```

### So what actually failed

Patchset 2 added a NEW block — the `_send` helper's docstring, which did not exist in
patchset 1 — and I wrote the sha into it with no ticket id, alias, or ADR anywhere in that
block. That is why the count went 3 -> 4. The gate failed **correctly, on text that did not
exist when CI voted**. No selection problem, no inconsistency between lanes.

### What stands

The edit itself stays: citing `emersed-specific-mutt` instead of the bare sha is what
AGENTS.md asks for and what the guard's acceptors are built around. Only the justification was
wrong, not the change.

### The habit that failed

I inferred a gap from "the guard failed locally on a tree CI passed" without checking whether
it was the same tree. It was not — my own new docstring was in it. This is the same error the
tautology check avoided: I ran the discriminating experiment on the mutation and it paid off,
and did not run one here. The check that would have settled it — fetch the patchset, run the
script — took under a minute.

The commit message does not carry this claim (verified against `git log -1 --format=%B`), so
no amend is needed for it; patchset 2 stands as pushed.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

Discovered while proving bug `5931-78a3-95d2-44cd` (marker dropped by truncation). The
Cloud outbound comment path fits the SAME body with TWO different rules, so the
body-equality dedup can never match for an over-length comment.

- **Differ / comparison key** — `outbound_comments._diff_comments` computes
  `sanitizer.fit_comment(body)`. Cloud's `_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment`
  (`adapters/jira/backend.py:152-154`) is `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body`, a
  PLAIN-CHARACTER cap at `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS = 32767`.
- **Send path** — `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.add_comment` fits with
  `AdfCodec.fit_outbound` -> `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit`, which measures the SERIALIZED
  ADF against `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT = 32000`.

## Runtime evidence

Driving both with a 40,000-char body (worktree `fix-illadopsis-marker`, repo venv):

```
compare key len:      32767
landed jira key len:  31887
BODY-EQUALITY SECONDARY SKIP HITS (today): False
```

The two keys can never be equal for any over-length comment.

## Why it matters

`emersed-specific-mutt` made the ID-based skip (`binding_store.is_comment_mapped` /
`jira_comment_id`) PRIMARY, so this is the belt-and-suspenders layer — but that layer is
exactly the guard against a lost map write (a crash between `add_comment` and
`record_comment_id`). For over-length comments it is structurally dead, so a lost map
write re-posts every pass. `comment_limits.py`'s own docstring states the convergence
requirement this violates: "If the two paths used different truncation logic they could
never agree on the landed body, and the loop would persist."

Not fixed under 5931 — that bug's fix is confined to preserving the marker and does not
change any comparison key. This divergence predates it and is unchanged by it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The differ's comment comparison key and the Cloud send path apply the identical fit.
- [ ] A test drives both and asserts the landed body equals the comparison key for an
      over-length comment (RED on current code).

## Fix plan (added after runtime confirmation on current main)

**Restore the shared-fitter invariant on the CLOUD side only.** `_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment`
becomes byte-identical to the text the Cloud send path actually lands — the same shape Data
Center already has (`_DCSanitizer.fit_comment` is pinned byte-identical to
`sanitize_comment`'s truncation).

1. `outbound_comments.py` — add `fit_comment_as_sent(text, fit)` beside `fit_preserving_marker`:
   the marker-free content the send path lands, i.e. `fit_preserving_marker(decorate(text), fit)`
   with the decoration removed. Backend-neutral: `fit` arrives as an injected
   `Callable[[str], str]`, exactly as `fit_preserving_marker` takes it, so the core module still
   names no vendor and no numeric limit. The decoration's separator length comes from
   `_decorate_outbound_comment` itself, so there is still one source of truth.
2. `adapters/jira/backend.py` — `_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment` returns
   `fit_comment_as_sent(body, AdfCodec(rich="cloud" in cutover_clients()).fit_outbound)`
   instead of `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body(body)`. Built exactly as `_fit_description`
   builds its codec, so the flag governs both.

**Deliberately NOT changed.** `_diff_comments` keeps calling `sanitizer.fit_comment` rather
than `codec.fit_outbound`: bug 049e makes Data Center's comment fitter deliberately distinct
from its description fitter, and coupling them in the shared layer would retarget DC's comment
ceiling to its description fitter. Data Center's `fit_comment`, its send path, and
`comment_limits.truncate_comment_body` are all untouched — so this does not absorb
`community-sediment-snipe` (DC outbound comments never length-fitted), which remains open and
separate.

## Blast radius — no key migration, no re-post storm

The dedup key is computed in memory on every pass and is never persisted (`binding_store`
stores `local_comment_key` -> Jira comment id, never a body or a body hash), so there is no
stored key to migrate.

Verified by driving the old key, the new key and the actual landed body over a corpus (short,
multi-line 20k, markdown, unicode, empty, 32,200, 31,800, 43k single-line, 60k multi-line) in
both rich modes: **every case where the old key matched the landed body, the new key matches it
too.** The change can only ADD dedup skips, never remove one, so no already-landed comment can
be re-posted as a result. Under the shipped default (`rich_text_cutover = off`) the new key
converges on the whole corpus; under this project's `cloud` setting the over-length cases still
diverge for an unrelated reason recorded on this ticket (the inbound decode asymmetry), which is
filed separately.

## Two existing tests must be RETARGETED (not weakened)

Both currently pin the model of the send path that commit `27b868ba55` invalidated, so both
pin the defect. Neither can hold alongside the restored invariant; each is rebuilt to derive
its expectation from the real send path so it cannot go stale the same way again, and each is
mutation-checked to confirm it still returns RED when the fix is reverted.

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_richtext_port_heldout.py::test_fit_comment_truncates_over_limit_byte_identical`
  asserts `sanitizer.fit_comment(huge) == comment_limits.truncate_comment_body(huge)` — a direct
  pin of the plain 32,767 cap. Rebuilt against `fit_preserving_marker(decorate(huge),
  AdfCodec.fit_outbound)`, keeping the "actually truncated" assertion and ADDING an assertion
  that the result is no longer the old cap.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py::test_oversize_comment_converges_over_two_passes`
  simulates the landed Jira body as `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body(emitted_body)`. That
  stale stub is why this "convergence" test stayed green while live convergence was broken.
  Rebuilt to call exactly what `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` calls.

file_impact.reason: RED oracle: differ key vs landed body
retarget: this oracle pins fit_comment to the superseded truncate_comment_body cap and must be rebuilt from the real send path
retarget: models the landed body as truncate_comment_body(emitted), stale since 27b868ba55; rebuild from the real send path

compiled_state.title: Cloud comment dedup key is fitted at 32767 while the send path fits at the 32000 ADF limit
